newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean stocks end higher on foreign demand.
newsitem.headline: Chilean stocks end higher on foreign demand.

text.p: Chilean stocks ended broadly higher in light turnover, with demand coming from abroad on a string of good first-quarter earnings, brokers said.

The bourse was quiet throughout the day due to Thursday's holiday. The IPSA index of the 40 most-traded shares closed 0.47 percent higher at 119.34 points, as did the general IGPA index at 5356.22 points on paltry volume of 7.2 billion pesos.

Brokers said Monday's inflation and jobless figures will set the tone for the market early next week. The official April consumer price index and January-to-March jobless figures are due to be released Monday.

Risers included stocks perceived to have had better-than-expected first quarter results, including copper mine Mantos Blancos, which ended 2.9 percent higher at 990 pesos, and copper products maker Manufacturas del Cobre, up 4.9 percent to 1,180 pesos.
Wood products maker Infodema was up 4.5 percent to 23 pesos after it jettisoned its heavily indebted subsidiary Tableros Nobel, selling it to competitor Maderas y Sinteticos (Masisa).
Pension fund administrator Provida was up 3.2 percent to 8,050 pesos.

The telecom sector has drawn renewed interest on the basis of first-quarter earnings. Telecom de Chile ended 1.2 percent higher at 3,300 pesos, but long-distance competitor Telex-Chile, which posted disappointing earnings, slipped 4.6 percent to 1,030 pesos.

Other decliners included agro-industrial concern Iansa, off two percent to 72 pesos after reporting a sharp drop in first-quarter earnings over the same period last year. Iansa's investment society, Campos, was also off, closing 2.3 percent down to 84 pesos.
